**Part I.** Substituting θ = π/6 into ρ²cos2θ = 8 gives ρ²·(1/2) = 8, so ρ² = 16 and ρ = ±4. The points are (4, π/6) and (−4, π/6), and the latter is the same point as (4, 7π/6). The submitted A(4, π/6), B(4, 7π/6) matches.

**Part II.** C₁ in Cartesian form is x² − y² = 8. Substituting the line gives t² + 4√3t − 8 = 0, so t₁ + t₂ = −4√3 and t₁t₂ = −8. Since (√3/2)² + (1/2)² = 1, t is an arc-length parameter, and |MN| = |t₁ − t₂| = √(48 + 32) = √80 = 4√5. This matches the submitted value.

The submitted write-up has a small typo in the Cartesian conversion (it writes x² + y²·(…) instead of (x² + y²)·(…)), but it still reaches x² − y² = 8, and the final answers are right.
